judged_text: updateEvent's fallback branch runs `.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the predicate can never match and the fallback always yields undefined where it previously returned destinationCalendar.externalId. Rescheduling any booking whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId (every booking created through the no-credentialId destination path in this diff) sends calendarId: undefined to calendar.events.update, which throws the missing-required-parameter error — the Google event is never moved to the new time.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the `updateEvent` fallback was changed from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. This fallback branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the `.find(...)` predicate compares against `undefined/null` and will almost always return `undefined`, losing the previous behavior of selecting the event’s destination calendar. The same broken pattern appears in `deleteEvent`/`calendarId` fallback. This is a concrete logic error introduced by the diff that can cause Google API calls to be made without a valid `calendarId` (or to fall back incorrectly), breaking updates/reschedules when `externalCalendarId` isn’t provided.
